researchLabGuide.title: How to Use MedHelp®
researchLabGuide.description: Use `meta-pipeline-planner` in Meta Chat first to start the systematic review pipeline, then review tasks and artifacts here in the Meta Workspace.
researchLabGuide.step1: Go to Meta Chat and ask the agent to prefer `meta-pipeline-planner` for your review topic, goal, or manuscript idea; only fall back to `meta-analysis-workflow` if it is unavailable.
researchLabGuide.step2: Answer the clarifying questions so the agent can define your research brief and pipeline correctly.
researchLabGuide.step3: The agent creates your research brief and stage-based task pipeline.
researchLabGuide.step4: Return to the Meta Workspace to review progress across literature, protocol, search, screening, extraction, statistics, figures, manuscript, and presentation outputs.
researchLabGuide.step5: Click Go to Meta Chat on any task to execute it, then refresh this page to inspect the latest Meta artifacts and keep the pipeline moving.
researchLabGuide.interfaceMap: Interface: task board on the left, Meta outputs and file preview on the right. Click an output to inspect it or Go to Meta Chat on any task to execute it.
researchLabGuide.readmeHint: For full process details, see README.md -> Usage Guide.
researchLabGuide.briefEditingStep1: Fill core constraints first (goal, boundaries, metrics). Incomplete inputs are acceptable for initial task generation.
researchLabGuide.briefEditingStep2: Click Apply Template + Generate Tasks to update the Meta brief and regenerate the task list.
researchLabGuide.briefEditingStep3: Use the "Use in Meta Chat" action from the Pipeline Task List below in sequence, and keep writing clarified conclusions back to the Meta brief.
researchLabGuide.collapsedHint: Guide hidden. Expand to view setup steps.

projectDashboard.automationPrompt: Use the meta-pipeline-planner skill to start this Meta project pipeline; use meta-analysis-workflow for cross-stage orchestration. Follow the project memory files, first identify the current stage, missing items, and next tasks; save the project startup report to 01_protocol/project_startup_report.md or a dated file in that folder; do not fabricate data, PDFs, extracted fields, or statistical results; when data/PDF/fields are unavailable, write a cannot-extract report; add targeted human-review checkpoints; after long runs, compact context by updating research_brief/tasks. If a research brief and task list already exist, continue the next task directly.
